title: Sealed Admin Change-Log Escrow for Residency-Aware Retention
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement a tamper-evident admin audit escrow that captures admin actions, access events, and configuration changes with residency-aware retention controls. The escrowed artifacts must be stored in an immutable (WORM) store, anchored with a cryptographic timestamp/HSM signature, and usable for automated compliance reporting and legal hold exports.
acceptance_criteria: All admin actions (role changes, policy edits, permission grants/revokes), privileged API calls, and config updates are emitted to the new audit stream with structured fields (actor, action_type, target, before, after, request_id, region, timestamp, tenant_id).
Audit records are sharded by region/tenant residency labels and written to a WORM-backed storage path with server-side immutability controls enforced for configured retention windows.
Each retention window supports retention policies per-region and per-tenant, with enforcement that prevents early deletion unless an approved legal hold/escrow release procedure is followed.
A periodic anchoring process bundles signed Merkle roots of daily records and submits an HSM-backed timestamp signature; signatures are stored alongside the sealed bundles and are verifiable offline.

Automated evidence export job can produce a verifiable bundle (records + Merkle proof + HSM signature) for a time range and tenancy, and a corresponding human-readable report summarizing scope, residency, and retention status.
Rollout includes a canary in staging and two customer tenants in production with monitoring for write latency, escrow write error rate <0.1%, and verification latency <30s for anchor operations.
Security review signoff completed and integration tests for tamper detection (e.g., modified object, missing anchor) present and passing.
design_notes: Opt for append-only segmented bundles (daily shards) rather than per-event immediate WORM writes to reduce small object churn and S3 lifecycle cost, while still enabling immutability via object-level WORM and server-side locks.

Each bundle is a compressed newline-delimited JSON (ndjson) file containing canonicalized audit events and a bundle manifest file describing schema version, event count, residency labels, and checksum.

Anchoring uses a Merkle tree over canonicalized events; compute Merkle root at bundle closure and send to a signing service that uses an HSM-backed key to produce a timestamped signature and public attestation. Store attestation metadata in the escrow manifest.

Residency is determined at ingestion time using tenant metadata and request routing region; records tagged with residency labels will only be exported to storage buckets that meet the residency constraint and are covered by retention settings.
Use existing event router pipeline for initial ingest with a dedicated sink for sealed-escrow bundles to reduce coupling with high-throughput runtime paths.

Design trade-off: batching reduces API latency amplification but increases time-to-immuability window. Chosen batching granularity: 5–15 minute closure for most tenants, configurable per customer/region/priority.
Provide an override path for immediate seal and anchor for legal-hold workflows; this will add synchronous work and should be rate-limited and audited separately.
Export format: verifiable bundle (ndjson bundle + manifest.json + signature.sig). Include an index file for fast lookup of event ranges and residency constraints.

Retention enforcement leverages a multi-layer approach: storage-level WORM + orchestration guard rails that prevent object deletion unless an approved release token is present (issued by the compliance service).
implementation_steps: 1) Schema: define canonical audit event schema and manifest spec; update runtime emitters to populate required fields.
2) Ingest: add sealed-escrow sink to event router; implement shard/segment writer with configurable closure interval and size limits.
3) Storage: provision WORM-enabled buckets per region; implement server-side immutability policies and access controls.
4) Anchoring: build merkle tree builder and HSM signing client; integrate with key management and timestamping service.
5) Evidence Export: implement export worker that collects bundles for a given time range/tenant, verifies signatures, and produces the verifiable bundle and summary report PDF/JSON.
6) Residency Enforcement: add routing rules to ensure bundles are written only to permitted regional buckets; add validation tests for cross-region leak scenarios.
7) Legal Hold: implement legal-hold API that pins bundles and prevents deletion; integrate approval workflow with compliance UI and audit trail.
8) Observability: emit metrics (bundle_write_latency, bundle_write_errors, anchor_latency, anchor_failures, export_duration), dashboards, and SLOs.
9) Security: complete threat modeling, key usage review, and internal pentest of the escrow workflow; document controls for key rotation and HSM access.
10) Tests: unit, integration (staging with tenant residency variations), and chaos tests (simulate partial writes, modified objects, and missing anchoring).
11) Rollout: staging canary -> internal prod tenants -> opt-in customer pilots -> gradual global enablement.
rollout_plan: Week 1: Feature branch + unit tests; deploy sealed-escrow sink to staging; validate canonical schema and shard closure behavior.
Week 2: Deploy anchoring service to staging; run end-to-end tests including HSM signing and verification.
Week 3: Internal canary in production for insight and config-change auditing only (no customer PII); monitor metrics and iterate.
Week 4-6: Pilot with two compliance-focused customers (APAC + EU) using residency labels and retention policies; gather feedback and harden export UX.
Week 7: Security signoff and runbook finalization; enable legal-hold override and release procedures.
Week 8: Gradual rollout to all tenants with default retention policy; provide communications and console toggle for admins.
Contingency: rollback path to stop generating new bundles and preserve existing escrow bundles if anchoring system exhibits >0.5% error rate over a 1-hour window.
monitoring_and_alerting: Alert: bundle_write_errors > 0.1% over 15m -> page oncall infra-team.
Alert: anchor_failures (HSM signing) > 5 in 10m -> trigger failover to queued retry and page security.
Dashboard: daily bundles written per region, average bundle size, anchor latency distribution, and export success rate.
Verification job: nightly re-check of random sample of bundles (integrity verification using stored signatures) and report on any anomalies.
Audit log: every manual legal-hold request and release must be recorded to an access-audit topic with immutable entries.
notes: This ticket focuses on engineering buildout; UX for console retention policy editing will be a separate PM ticket but we will provide the API and hooks.
Coordinate with legal for retention durations and with security for KMS/HSM provisioning timelines.
Ensure the export format is compatible with e-discovery workflows used by enterprise compliance teams (indexing, proof verification steps).
